title: Trace-driven dashboard prioritization and metric definitions (cost-sensitive inference) - draft
body:
Context and purpose:

This is a working document to align on a smaller set of dashboard surfaces and metric definitions that are driven by trace signals and cost-sensitivity for token-serving inference. Focus is on prioritizing what to build in Q4 to reduce investigation time for performance degradations and to make cost tradeoffs visible to product owners.

Why a trace-first approach?
- Traces give request-scoped context (model, route, config, route policy, fallback) which is required to make sense of aggregate metrics that mix heterogeneous workloads.
- We can preferentially sample traces for high-cost or high-severity flows to keep traces informative without blowing budget.
- Trace anchors (start/end, model-variant-switch, kv-cache-miss, fallback) map cleanly to dashboard widgets and playbooks.

Goals for the prototype dashboard set:
1) Reduce Mean Time To Investigate (MTTI) for tail latency and error incidents by 40% using trace-linked widgets.
2) Surface cost-influence signals (tokens per call, batching efficiency, cache hit-rate) in the same view as latency.
3) Provide a lightweight drilldown path from aggregate SLOs -> top offending trace patterns -> session reconstruction.

Prioritized metric candidates (definitions and rationale)
- invocation.count: count of user-facing inference requests received (filtered by route). Rationale: baseline traffic.
- tokens.requested_per_invocation.p50/p90/p99: distribution of input tokens. Used to detect shifts in prompt lengths causing latency/cost regressions.
- tokens.generated_per_invocation.p50/p90/p99: output-side distribution. Useful when model updates change verbosity.
- cpu_ms.per_token.p90: CPU work normalized by token output (compute proxy for on-host CPU pressure).
- gpu_ms.per_token.p90: GPU time normalized per token (when available from runtime).
- end_to_end.latency.p50/p90/p99/p99.9: full request latency from gateway to final response. Important SLI.
- model_inference.latency.p50/p90/p99: time spent in model exec only (excludes network/proxy).
- kv_cache.hit_rate.percent: percent of requests served from prefix/KV cache.
- batching.utilization.percent: average batch size / target batch size (helps explain latency vs cost tradeoffs).
- fallback.rate.per_1k: rate of automatic fallbacks to cheaper/slower model variants.
- cost.per_invocation.usd: token-based cost estimate for the call (approximation: input_tokens*model_input_unit_price + output_tokens*model_output_unit_price).
- cost.tail_concentration.p95: fraction of total cost accounted for by top 5% of invocations over an interval.

Metric priming notes (how to compute consistently)
- Always include route, customer_tier, model_version, region, and cache_key hash as tags.
- Use consistent windowing semantics (1m, 5m, 1h) and report both point-in-time and rolling-24h baselines.
- Pxx should be computed using reservoir sketches for large cardinality; store both exact per-route p99 (when low-cardinality) and sketch for global.

Trace anchors and span design guidance
- Root span: inference.request received at gateway (tags: route, api_key_hash, region).
- Span: auth/check -> routing -> batching -> model.exec -> kv_cache.lookup -> result-merge -> response.write.
- Key attributes to attach: model_variant, quantization_profile, batch_size, batch_queue_delay_ms, kv_cache_hit (bool), fallback_reason.
- Add a cost_estimate attribute to root span (approx token_cost_usd).

Sampling policy suggestion (cost-aware hybrid)
- Always sample 100% of traces where cost_estimate > threshold_a (e.g., > $0.125).
- Always sample 100% where end_to_end.latency > p99_threshold for route.
- Probabilistic sampling for normal traffic: 0.1% global baseline, but boosted to 5% for routes with high cost_per_invocation.
- Ensure we keep a small consistent sample per customer (e.g., 1 trace per 1k invocations) to enable long-term baselines.

Dashboard wireframe notes (three views)
1) Overview (for on-call +engineering)
- Single-row: invocation.count, cost.per_invocation.avg, cost.tail_concentration.p95, end_to_end.latency.p99, kv_cache.hit_rate, fallback.rate.
- Heatmap: p99 latency by route x region (color = relative change vs baseline).
- Top contributing traces to cost (list with quick link to trace).

2) Investigator view (for SRE/Serving runtime)
- Time-series: batch_queue_delay_ms, batching.utilization, model_inference.latency.p99 aligned with errors and fallback.rate.
- Trace-sample panel: show 10 recent traces matching spike criteria with annotated span waterfall.
- Quick filters: by model_version, quantization_profile, route.

3) Product-level cost/quality view (for PMs/Finance)
- Cost per 100k invocations broken down by model_version + quantization_profile.
- Trend: output_tokens_per_invocation.p90 vs user-visible response quality metric (if available).
- Alerts: weekly cost growth > 15% for a route without commensurate increase in retention/engagement.

Alerting and playbook links
- Primary SLO: end_to_end.latency.p99 < route_SLO (per-route). Alert on sustained breach for 5m.
- Cost spike alert: sudden increase in cost.per_invocation.p95 top-3 routes change > 30% vs 24h baseline.
- Playbook: link traces to suspected root cause (cache-miss wave, batch drain, quantization fallback).

Rollout plan (MVP -> Q4 complete)
- Week 1: instrument trace anchors and add attributes to existing spans (batch_queue_delay_ms, cost_estimate). Owner: Ravi.
- Week 2: implement sampling policy and small persistent trace store for high-cost traces. Owner: Leah.
- Week 3: metric calculation for tokens.* and cost.* (sketch-backed). Owner: Maya.
- Week 4: wireframe dashboard + link traces -> handoff doc + initial on-call runbook. Owner: eng-observability.

Open questions / tradeoffs
- Cost_estimate accuracy vs complexity: lightweight token-pricing model vs pre-aggregated billing join.
- Privacy: avoid logging full prompt text in spans; use hashed prompt signatures for dedupe.
- Sketch vs exact: for high-cardinality (route+customer) we may need hybrid approach.
- Should we expose cost.per_invocation to customers? (product decision, potential misuse).

Quick experiments to validate hypotheses
- 1-week A/B: enable full sampling for top-10 highest-cost routes and verify trace utility for root cause resolution.
- 2-day: inject synthetic large-prompt traffic on staging to validate batching.utilization and batch_queue_delay_ms correlation with p99 latency.

Next steps / action items
- Finalize naming conventions for metric keys (Maya).
- Create Jira tickets for instrumentation (Ravi).
- Draft playbook skeleton for common root causes and trace-based triage (Leah).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider adding a "session replay" light-weight event that concatenates span ids to rebuild cross-request journeys for multi-turn chat.
- Think about an API to request higher sampling on-demand for a customer when a support ticket is opened.

References and background links:
- Related: CONFLUENCE-obs/metric-roots (see signal taxonomy)
- Related GH PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/42

Draft status: rough. Use this to scope the MVP for the next telemetry sprint.
